body: Matsumoto, Pronk and Roelofsen, 'What Makes Conference Calls Useful? The Information Content of Managers' Presentations and Analysts' Discussion Sessions' (The Accounting Review 86(4), 2011; ~700 Crossref citations), more than 10,000 US call transcripts. Both the presentation and the Q&A contain incremental information beyond the press release, but the discussion (Q&A) segment is relatively more informative, and more so with higher analyst following. When performance is poor, managers disclose more in the presentation, but even more information comes out in the Q&A. Related: Mayew-Venkatachalam (vocal stress) and Larcker-Zakolyukina (deception cues), already summarised in insight:text-tone-research-summary. Hollander, Pronk and Roelofsen (2010) find that managers who refuse to answer questions ('silence') see negative price reactions. Replicated: consistent with later US and European studies. For India, Jain-Khizer-Thirumalai find tone in calls moves prices but does not predict operating performance (insight:india-concall-tone-cheap-talk). Use for us: when reading Indian concalls, score the Q&A rather than the opening speech. Note which questions are deflected ('we will not give guidance', 'let us take it offline'), which numbers are given only when pushed, and whether the same question recurs each quarter, which signals a persistent problem. Store dodged questions in the promise tracker as negative evidence.

data.finding: Q&A more informative than presentation; more so with analyst following and poor performance

title: Earnings calls: the Q&A carries more information than the prepared remarks (Matsumoto-Pronk-Roelofsen 2011)

body: Validated on SUNFLAG plus two seeded-random no-concall NSE small caps (GULFPETRO, REPRO). Annual reports carry few checkable promises: hand reads found 7 (GULFPETRO FY25) and 8 (REPRO FY25) forward statements, almost all undated; the pipeline recovered 3/7 and 2/8 at the promise stage (zone 5/7, 3/8). Auto-scored n was 5 (SUNFLAG), 0, 0. The most useful AR-mode outputs are not the MCS but (1) the asset status tracker (SUNFLAG: 17/17 hand-ledger mine-status cells reproduced; the unchanged Belgaon 5.391 MT reserve flagged) and (2) disclosure-quality flags: stale forward dates at filing (REPRO x3), 'done during the year' text repeated across years (SUNFLAG Blooming mill), identical sentences copied year to year. Treat AR-mode MCS as non-comparable with concall MCS. Research, not advice.
title: Promise tracker AR mode (no-concall companies): what annual reports can and cannot score (Nov 2026)
